All cases now validate correctly. Here's the function, saved to `validate_email.py`:

```python
import re

LOCAL_PART = r"[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*"
DOMAIN_LABEL = r"[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"

EMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(
    rf"^{LOCAL_PART}@{DOMAIN_LABEL}(?:\.{DOMAIN_LABEL})+$"
)


def is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(email, str) or len(email) > 254:
        return False
    return EMAIL_PATTERN.match(email) is not None
```

It checks: proper local-part/domain structure, no leading/trailing/double dots, valid domain labels (no leading/trailing hyphens, ≤63 chars each), a TLD present, and the overall 254-char RFC length limit. It's not full RFC 5322 compliance (nothing practical is), but covers the real-world cases well. Tested against 7 cases including edge cases like `<email>` and `<email>` — all correct.
